context:
Goal: the Stop hook refuses to end a turn with an open CI wait and no check-in, without false alarms or misses.
Problem (rule): the check counts CronCreate as a check-in, and any check-in covers the wait. The root rule says "check-in", not a tool, and describes a one-time check-in that fires once. The coordinator picked keep (2026-11-14 11:07 CST, undoable); you have not been asked.
Based on (code, lane's read, unchecked by triage): test CI05 in hooks/test_stall_watch_stop.py pins the four-tool count.
Based on (ruling): own-ci-wait-subscribe-guard (owner 21:39 CST Nov 13, relayed): subscribe or poll first; check-ins are the safety net. It names no tool.
Departs from: main — it names send_later only in the remedy text; the lane counts four tools (option a) or one (option b).
Meanwhile: the lane keeps option a as a recorded Limit in decision ci-wait-reads-run-status and does not wait for you.
Option a is the lane's and the coordinator's pick but is not starred: it widens what the check accepts (four tools where the text names one), and a widening is never starred.
Your question, 15:01 CST Nov 14: "are these my only options and which is good and why?" Triage's answer (a reading, not your word): not the only ones in principle. A third shape counts the one-time tools (send_later, ScheduleWakeup) and refuses a recurring CronCreate. Whether the check can tell a one-time call from a recurring one is unread; triage asked the coordinator. Of the two shown: b matches the rule text and does not widen, and its cost is that sessions on create_trigger or ScheduleWakeup are blocked at Stop until they also set a send_later. a is the lane's and the coordinator's pick, blocks nothing, and widens, so it carries the line above and is not starred. Nothing waits on this item.
Update 15:11 CST Nov 14 (coordinator's grep, not a read of the check): hooks on main name send_later only in hooks/shared_names.py line 23 (a name list) and CronCreate only in a comment in hooks/test_local_time.py line 1542; it found no code that tells a recurring cron from a one-time one. No lane that read the Stop check is in its notes. So whether a third shape is buildable is unknown.
Your question, 18:37 CST Nov 14: "is B better but just needs to be better thought out?" Triage's answer (a reading, not a measure; you have not picked): on the rule text, yes: b matches the remedy text and the one-time check-in the rule describes, and it widens nothing. And yes, it needs more thought: its price is that a session that waits with create_trigger or ScheduleWakeup is blocked at Stop until it also sets a send_later, and how many sessions do that is unmeasured. The third shape (count one-time tools, refuse a recurring cron) is unbuilt, and whether the check can tell them apart is unknown. A lane could measure which tools sessions use to wait and read whether the check can tell one-time from recurring, then bring b or the third shape back to you. No star: a widens, and no session recommends b. The coordinator is asked for its view. Nothing waits.
Update 18:43 CST Nov 14: Source: coordinator's Explore read (read-only Sonnet agent, hooks/stall_watch.py, hooks/guard.py and step ci-wait-stop-needs-checkin at local main af2c312c, shallow, later edits unknown); unverified by triage; the coordinator did not read this item's text. Stop check, coordinator's Explore read, unverified by triage: it counts send_later, create_trigger, CronCreate and ScheduleWakeup as a check-in (stall_watch.py:862, tests CI03-CI06). It reads only the tool name (:975), never run_once_at, cron_expression or recurring, so a recurring check-in passes; only the remedy text says one-time. It reads the transcript only and keeps ONE wait, the newest ready call. The 55-minute cap (guard.py, ci_wait_cap.json) guards only send_later with CI wording. Cost: no new process, file or timer. Usage by sessions is unmeasured except list_triggers at 18:41 CST Nov 14: 2 one-shot, 0 recurring, both runner 10's check-ins. The coordinator recommends NEITHER a nor b. It proposes a new option c, added below: keep all four tools but read each call's input. It narrows what passes, so it widens nothing, and it is starred at the coordinator's recommendation. b (send_later only) would block runner 10's create_trigger check-ins, the only measured ones. Your pick. Nothing waits.
CLOSED 20:20 CST Nov 14 on the COORDINATOR'S pick, option d (added by triage from the coordinator's words: send_later only for session waits; the four tools stay for event waits a session cannot poll), taken under the owner's 20:18 CST Nov 14 words ("Nothing can't be undone don't wait on me") (owner words relayed by the consultant 20:20; the pick is the coordinator's, undoable, not the owner's own). The star on c stays as recorded at the time (the coordinator's earlier recommendation, 18:46); the coordinator then chose d. How the check tells a session wait from an event wait is unbuilt and unread. Ruling coord-837-d-send-later-session-waits. If you disagree, say so and it reopens.

short: Which tools count as a check-in for the Stop check: four, or send_later only?
title: Does any of four scheduling tools count as the check-in the Stop check wants (a), or only send_later, which the remedy text names (b)?
why: The rule says "check-in", not a tool. The lane's check counts CronCreate as one, and a recurring cron is not the one-time check-in the rule describes.
